sections.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's $L^2$ conjecture
sections.abstract: For every dimension d≥2 and 0≤σ<1/3, the authors construct a smooth bounded nonnegative potential with arbitrarily small weighted L² size for which −Δ+V has only pure point spectrum at positive energies.
sections.claimed_result: The authors say their lens-type potential disproves Barry Simon's conjecture that the stated weighted-square-integrability condition forces an absolutely continuous component of infinite multiplicity at almost every positive energy.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Schrödinger operators on R^d, d≥2, with smooth, bounded, nonnegative potentials; the construction covers 0≤σ<1/3 and can make both the supremum norm and the specified weighted integral arbitrarily small.
sections.unique_caveat: The result does not cover the endpoint σ=1/3 or sign-changing potentials; the authors disclose LLM assistance in developing the construction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An independent math.SP feed posted the paper title alongside another spectral-theory preprint; the result directly challenges a named conjecture and is cross-listed in spectral theory and mathematical physics.

sections.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
sections.abstract: The authors construct a non-Gaussian, distribution-valued critical solution of the two-dimensional KPZ equation as a limit of centered log partition functions for Gaussian directed polymers and through a renormalized Cole–Hopf transform of the critical stochastic heat flow.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify a critical process that is non-Gaussian, has a log-log covariance blow-up near the spatial diagonal, and exhibits Gaussian fluctuations after averaging on shrinking spatial scales.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is the critical two-dimensional KPZ equation, interpreted through Gaussian directed polymers and a renormalized Cole–Hopf transform of the critical stochastic heat flow.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an 84-page preprint whose authors describe extensive generative-AI input; the limiting construction and technical arguments require specialist scrutiny.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A claimed critical scaling-limit construction with linked polymer and stochastic-heat-flow formulations, plus reported covariance and small-scale fluctuation results, spans probability and mathematical physics.

sections.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4/3 n
sections.abstract: For every thrackle on n≥4 vertices, the author proves an upper bound of floor(4(n−1)/3) edges, using a finite computer-assisted verification and a discharging argument.
sections.claimed_result: For finite simple thrackleable graphs on n≥4 vertices, the author proves m≤floor(4(n−1)/3), improving the coefficient in previous general upper bounds.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A thrackle is a plane drawing in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing; the theorem is for finite simple graphs.
sections.unique_caveat: The result improves an upper bound but does not prove Conway's conjectured m≤n; its argument incorporates a computer-assisted check for small graphs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete improvement to the best-known linear bound on a prominent extremal-graph conjecture, with combinatorics and two topology cross-lists; the paper specifies the computational and discharging ingredients.

sections.title: Aleshin graphs are expanders
sections.abstract: The authors prove that Aleshin level graphs are two-sided expanders, establish linear diameter bounds for Aleshin and Bellaterra graph families, and give explicit spectral-gap and edge-expansion lower bounds.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain normalized spectral gap at least 1−2√2/3 and edge-expansion constant at least 3−2√2 for Aleshin graphs, and show that undirected Aleshin graphs are not Ramanujan for n≥10.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The claims concern the specified levels of the Aleshin and Bellaterra graph families, whose level-n vertex count is 2^n.
sections.unique_caveat: These estimates concern particular automaton-generated graph families; they do not establish comparable bounds for arbitrary finite graphs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A claimed resolution of the Malyshev–Pak conjecture with explicit constants, alongside improved diameter growth, gives a concrete combinatorial result rather than a topic-only signal.

sections.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed–Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
sections.abstract: The author classifies deep holes for interpolation-degree offsets m=3,4,5,6,7 over every finite field and proves uniform bounds for arbitrary m≥3, with explicit exceptional families in two characteristic-two cases.
sections.claimed_result: For m∈{3,4,5,6,7} it gives all deep-hole cases over finite fields; it also supplies field-size-dependent exclusions/classifications for arbitrary m≥3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Full-length Reed–Solomon code RS_q(k) and received words whose interpolation polynomial has degree k+m; the broad uniform bounds require the explicit inequalities on q stated in the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: The exact unconditional classification is limited to m≤7; the general-m results have field-size and parity conditions, and some finite cases use supplied computation certificates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states exact classifications without a field-size hypothesis for five offsets, general uniform bounds, and cross-listing across coding theory, combinatorics, and number theory.

sections.title: A semiampleness result for hyperkähler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
sections.abstract: For a smooth hyperkähler fourfold with Picard group generated by a nontrivial nef non-big line bundle of nonnegative Kodaira dimension, the authors prove that some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration.
sections.claimed_result: Under the stated hypotheses, a positive tensor power of the line bundle induces a Lagrangian fibration; the proof uses an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing theorem for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: X is a smooth hyperkähler fourfold; Pic(X) is generated by a nef, nontrivial, non-big line bundle L and κ(L)≥0.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem retains the Picard-rank-one and nonnegative-Kodaira-dimension hypotheses; it does not establish semiampleness for every nef non-big class.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A stated semiampleness theorem with a geometric proof and three algebraic-geometric/differential-geometric categories; the authors also identify unobstructedness and smoothing results as tools of independent interest.

sections.title: Nonvanishing of 2-primary Kolyvagin classes via simultaneous quadratic twists
sections.abstract: Under explicit Galois-image and cohomological hypotheses, the author constructs simultaneous quadratic twists of an elliptic curve with controlled 2-Selmer dimensions and proves nonvanishing and order results for associated standard 2-primary Kolyvagin classes.
sections.claimed_result: The author constructs a terminal twist whose Kummer class is the standard mod-2 Kolyvagin class, obtains an exact 2-adic index formula, and gives nonvanishing criteria and higher-order conclusions under additional hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: An elliptic curve E/Q, an imaginary quadratic field satisfying the Heegner hypothesis with D<−4, a fixed modular parametrization, surjectivity modulo 2^L for L≥2, and a cohomological exclusion at level 4.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions are conditional on the stated arithmetic hypotheses and use low-corank 2-converse and 2-primary BSD inputs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a construction linking quadratic twists, Selmer groups, Kolyvagin classes, and a 2-primary BSD formula, a substantive number-theoretic chain of results.

sections.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
sections.abstract: The author proves positive triple quantum Pieri and structure-constant formulas for quantum double Schubert polynomials, extends comparison/reduction formulas, and describes verified algorithms for computing products beyond previous methods.
sections.claimed_result: Triple quantum Schubert structure constants are polynomials in variable differences with nonnegative integer coefficients; the paper also proves a triple quantum Pieri formula and extends established comparison formulas.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The results concern quantum double Schubert polynomials and their structure constants in the stated flag-variety/quantum-Schubert setting; the paper's comment identifies a positivity appendix by Tongren Xiao and Yihua Yue.
sections.unique_caveat: The formulas apply to this specific quantum Schubert calculus framework; the abstract does not claim a general positivity theorem for arbitrary Schubert products.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract links explicit positivity formulas and quantum Bruhat graph chains with an implemented computational package; the result connects algebraic geometry and combinatorics.
